findings.message: Under StrictMode, every delete in the running app may log two 'removed' activity entries, because deleteItem queues a state update from inside another state updater; the new delete-activity test cannot catch this. deleteItem calls `setActivities(prevAct => [activity, ...prevAct])` inside the `setItems(prev => {...})` updater. src/main.tsx wraps <App /> in <StrictMode>, and React runs updater functions twice in development. The new test 'adds activity when deleting an item' uses renderHook without StrictMode, so it checks only the single-invocation case.

The new test locks in a fragile pattern without catching its bug. `deleteItem` calls `setActivities` inside the `setItems` updater function. The app runs under `<StrictMode>` (src/main.tsx:7), and in development React calls updater functions twice, so each delete adds two 'removed' activities. `renderHook` here doesn't use StrictMode, so the test passes anyway. Move the activity side effect out of the updater (find the item from current `items`, then call both setters), and/or render the hook with a StrictMode wrapper. Editing an item through the new Edit flow writes no activity entry, so the Recent Activity feed shows adds and deletes but never edits. updateItem only calls setItems and never calls setActivities. addItem (line 38) and deleteItem (line 74) both log activity, and ActivityEntry.action in src/types/inventory.ts already includes 'updated'. The diff wires updateItem to the new Edit button (App.tsx `onUpdate={updateItem}`) without adding a log entry, and no test covers edit activity.

This PR connects `updateItem` to the UI, but `updateItem` never adds an activity entry. `ActivityEntry.action` already has an `'updated'` value (src/types/inventory.ts:26), and add and delete both log to the feed. Edits made through the new Edit button won't show up in the activity feed, so the audit trail is incomplete. Add an `'updated'` activity in `updateItem` and test it, the same way this PR added a test for delete. The diff does not modify src/hooks/useInventory.ts. deleteItem's 'removed' activity logging (lines 57-78) already exists, so 'adds activity when deleting an item' passes before and after the change.

If the modal is ever given editItem without onUpdate, Save silently creates a duplicate item instead of failing, because onUpdate is optional and the code falls back to onAdd. `if (isEditMode && editItem && onUpdate) { onUpdate(editItem.id, form) } else { onAdd(form) }`, with `onUpdate?:` optional in AddItemModalProps. InventoryPage always passes onUpdate today, so the current app does not hit this path.

In edit mode, if `onUpdate` isn't provided (it's optional in the props), submitting silently falls through to `onAdd(form)`. That creates a duplicate item, with a new id, instead of updating the existing one. Edit mode should require `onUpdate` (make it required whenever `editItem` is set, or don't fall back to add), so a wiring mistake can't duplicate data. The component is still named AddItemModal but now handles both add and edit, and the README still describes it only as the 'add item modal'. `export default function AddItemModal({ isOpen, onClose, onAdd, editItem, onUpdate })` switches its heading and button text on `isEditMode`. README.md line 39 reads 'Inventory table, add item modal, status badges'.

The new Edit button sits directly beside a Delete button that removes the item in one click with no confirmation or undo, which makes an accidental, unrecoverable delete more likely. The diff inserts the Edit button (`className="mr-1 ..."`) right before `<button onClick={() => onDelete(item.id)}`. deleteItem filters the item out of state immediately, and there is no confirm step or restore path.
